Emma: Hi team — customer reported a Python streaming call that works for a few seconds then the generator just never yields again after an auth refresh. They see partial token/JSON and the SSE generator hangs. Repro steps below, any quick ideas? :thinking:

Raj: Can you paste the minimal repro and the SDK version + auth method?

Emma: Using redwood-python 1.2.4, OAuth short-lived token (expires 30s), rotating via our auth proxy. Quick repro: call .stream() on Chat interface and rotate token mid-stream. Example:```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(token=fetch_token())
def stream():
    for chunk in client.chat.stream(model="rwd-3b", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}]):
        print(chunk)

# run stream() and then trigger auth-proxy to swap token while stream is active
```
Logs we got: partial SSE payload then nothing:```
event: message
data: {"id":"tok_abc","delta":"Hello wo"
# connection stays open, no further data
# client generator loop doesn't resume
```

Lisa: This sounds like an SSE parse boundary issue when the auth refresh causes the upstream to send a 401/retry handshake and our client side attempts to reattach without emitting an error. Which transport are they using (requests, httpx, aiohttp)?

Emma: They reported using requests (sync). The auth-proxy returns 200 then switches token mid-TCP session (we do token swap via proxy rewriting headers). No explicit 401. The server logs show a new auth header received and then continued stream.

Mike: Huh. If the proxy rewrites headers mid-connection the server might be doing a restart behind the scenes (connection-level), producing a truncated SSE line. Our SSE parser expects lines ending in "\n\n" and if it sees EOF mid-line it should raise and close generator. It sounds like we swallow the socket close and keep generator alive.

Emma: Right — customer sees no exception, just generator hang. They tried adding timeouts on their side but the SDK read loop doesn't surface a BrokenPipeError or EOF.

Lisa: Can you ask them to run with env var RW_SDK_SSE_DEBUG=1 to capture raw frames? Also which pip package exactly? (there's a 1.2.5 pre-release with a socket-EOF fix)

Emma: They are on 1.2.4 (non-prerelease). I'll ask them to try 1.2.5b1. Meanwhile here's a minimal raw capture they sent (trimmed):```
:keepalive

data: {"delta":"Hello wo"

:heartbeat
```
After that the connection shows no more TCP payloads.

Raj: If the client doesn't get socket close then its internal buffer may still be waiting for the remainder of the event delimiter. Suggest adding a read-timeout fallback in SDK: if no '\n\n' after X seconds, yield partial and raise. But that's a change. For immediate help ask customer to restart stream on token rotation or use a short-lived reconnect strategy.

Lisa: Quick workaround (customer-level): detect your auth rotation event and restart the stream proactively when you swap tokens. For SDK fix, I'll open a ticket to ensure incomplete SSE events time out and raise a clear error.

Mike: Also ask them to try httpx+async path — async client uses different buffering behaviour and may show the EOF. Worth checking if the hang is only on requests sync transport.

Emma: Customer tried httpx async and saw the generator raise ConnectionResetError — so that path surfaces an error. Only requests sync was silent.

support-bot: New support ticket created: #SUP-8942 (linked to thread) :white_check_mark:

Raj: OK good signal. Can you collect the following and attach to the ticket: full raw capture (pcap or tcpdump), SDK logs with RW_SDK_SSE_DEBUG, Python version, requests version, and proxy config. Also please note exact time of token swap.

Emma: Will do. I've asked the customer for tcpdump and logs. They can repro in ~15s so should be easy to capture.

Lisa: I'll draft a unit test that simulates mid-event stream truncation + proxy header swap. If we can reproduce we can add explicit timeouts and an error like "SSEPartialEventError" so callers can fallback.

Mike: Filing an eng-runtime ticket too in case the server side has a behavior we should tolerate. cc @raj

Emma: Thanks all. I'll update #SUP-8942 once we have captures. For now workaround documented: restart stream on token rotation. :thumbsup:

Raj: Thanks — assign to eng-sdk if you get a consistent repro.

Emma: Marking as high priority for the customer (production flow).
